Chasing the Sun 2

By: Sinethemba Nogude | Paid

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
From a sport defined by its past, and a country defined by its differences, comes the story of a team that chooses to believe in something more.

“Chasing the Sun” is a powerful SuperSport documentary made in collaboration with the Springboks and tells the rousing tale of their path to redemption and World Cup glory in 2023.





The famous triumph remains a powerful memory, but the story behind the famous win is perhaps even more remarkable.

SuperSport was granted unprecedented access to the Springboks both in the build-up and during the tournament which helped produce incredible behind-the-scenes footage that goes to the heart of what it took to claim the Webb Ellis Cup last year.

“Chasing the Sun” is no ordinary story. It is a story about changing fortunes and changing mindsets, about pressure and hope, about recognizing the power of inspiration, and learning what representation truly means.

The moving documentary charts the Boks’ rise f to the pinnacle of international rugby, so vividly demonstrated when captain Siya Kolisi lifted the trophy in France .

With unprecedented access and exclusive contributions from coaching staff, players and commentators, the documentary is the story of how a team, a nation and the world came to discover that we are all indeed stronger together. “Chasing the Sun” is infused with humour, technical insights and emotional engagement that will reveal the Springboks like never before.

Script:


1. V/O A Rugby World Cup etched in the memories of every South African for years to come.

2. V/O From an agonizing defeat…

3. V/O To heart-stopping victories…the 2023 tournament had it all!

[Dramatic dip to black]
Link: The 2023 World Cup was the most dramatic and controversial, but also the toughest. So how did the Springboks win it?
4. V/O A collaboration between SuperSport and the Springboks, “Chasing the Sun 2” is a gripping five-part documentary series, that follows the Bok's toughest Rugby World Cup campaign ever - culminating in glory on that historic night in Paris.
5. V/O With unlimited access, a film crew shadowed the team for two years… leading up to the 2023 Rugby World cup - capturing remarkable behind-the-scenes moments.
6. V/O A sequel to the acclaimed ‘Chasing The Sun’ documentary series - which captured the Springboks' triumph in Japan in 2019 - this time, it's set to be even more captivating.
Upsound Lungani 04:36 08: 08 There's things that the public just hasn't seen, and even when we saw them for the first time, we were stunned.
7. V/O For head writer Lungani Zama, Chasing the Sun 2 will transcend the game of rugby.
Upsound Lungan 15:00i: it's become more than just the Springboks and the T1 rugby field, it's their relationship with the people that support themresponsibility that they feel they hold to the little boy and girl that's growing up wanting to be a Springbok or just wanting to make a difference in South Africa., the Springboks, are a reflection of South African attitude, perseverance, belief.
8. V/O The film crew travelled across the country, capturing unique stories of everyday South Africans…and some untold tales of their beloved Bokke.
Upsound Lungani We've covered most of the provinces. We've gone from Queenstown to Welkom toi, Amstelhof and Paarl. to KZN a very important element of telling the story is to be in the communities where these players come from.
9. V/O Even the toughest Springbok can get overwhelmed by a film crew. While they're used to pressure on the field, facing cameras is a whole different ball game. Bok centre Jesse Kriel.
Upsound Govan Question: 03:27. So, I mean, you guys had a camera crew the whole time?
Upsound Jesse Kriel 01:30 Yeah,I don't think a lot of people understand and see what actually goes into the preparation leading up into a test match,, the emotions, the mental, the mental side, all the coaching, the strategy and all the hard work that goes in. So it was nice to suppose, give people a glimpse of that.
Upsound Mzwandile Stick 03:08 I'm not a movie star so I wouldn't try to be to look nice or fancy around the cameras you know my job is to coach rugby.
10. V/O Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick, hopes the series will reveal how unexpected leaders emerged… and found their voice.
Upsound Mzwandile stickThe moments you're going to see probably in chasing the sun too, you know, Peter Steph in the changing room where he was taking over. people always think that Siya as a captain always makes decisions. we've got a lot of great leaders in our team. And there are very, very touchy moments in that changing room.
[breather]
Link: What makes this World Cup exceptional is the obstacles that the Springboks had to overcome to actually get to the final. Never mind win it
11. V/O The team grappled with a string of injury setbacks, testing their resilience and depth.
Upsound Govan 18:42 like when Maphimpi, when Malcolm Marks got injured. How did you guys react?
Upsound Jesse Kriel 18:50 it's a squad effort, and that's what we always speak about. On the podium at the end, when we won, everyone got their medal, all 33 players. So, and I was in the same position in 2019. I got injured in the first game, but I still won together with the team.
12 V/0 For team doctor Jerome Mampane, Makazole Maphimpi's fractured eye socket was particularly devastating.
Upsound Jerom Mamphane 40: 19 I think I was messed up after Maphimpi’s injury. So you take a player off the field, you can see he's clearly injury this probably means it's the end of his World Cup. Then your head says how old is Maphimpi ? Can he really make the next World Cup? I said look I think you're out for six weeks and Probably that's the first time I saw Maphimpi cry.
[breather]
13. V/O From gruelling training sessions to intense matches, the film crew captured every heart-stopping moment… Including the pulsating knockout game against the hosts, France.
[quarterfinal upsound]
Upsound Govan 20:24 The quarter-final especially, was tough, right?
Upsound Jesse 20:39 Yeah So I think it was more mindset going in there knowing that listen we've got a job to do here and all the things are going to be stacked against us and those are all things that we can't control.
[breather Cheslin Charge down]
Upsound Govan: How did the team react on the field when Cheslin charged down that.
Upsound Jesse 21:25 That was unreal, you don't see that often, just having that awareness to even think about that on such a massive occasion, Just shows what a rugby player he is... That's a thing about having the right people in the team.
Upsound Mzwandile Stick 19:53 It's not something that comes from us as coaches. everyone understands that Cheslin Kobe is a special player with stepping and all the other stuff. But they don't realize that this is a guy that also does a lot of hard work off the field.
[final whistle]
14. V/O In moments of near defeat, the team dug deep… into what it means to be a Springbok, and to be South African.
Upsound Govan 25:15 That semi-final. I'll be honest. I had to switch the TV off, go to the kitchen, come back and Pollard kicked it over.
Upsound Mzwandile Stick 26:07 A lot of things that we've planned didn't go according to the plan. 26:33We had to make sure that from the top, we change our strategy. If you remember very well, we also had a meeting there during the game as a coaching staff, where we had to tweak things around in some of our departments.
[tension with upsounds of the game]
15. V/O To our collective relief, the bokke held their nerve.
Jesse Kriel 22:22 Yeah, the ice man. I had to bet my house and everything that I have on someone to kick a goal, it would be him for him to come back into the squad and make and make such an awesome contribution was just speaks volumes of the kind of player he is. And the coolness he has.
[breather]
Link By now, the Springbok coaching staff have proven themselves to be true rugby innovators. But how do they come up with these tactics?
16. V/O From Rassie's creative use of traffic light signals on the sidelines… to the notorious 7-1 bench strategy, with forwards dominatin.rugby fans will finally gain insight into the coaching team's strategy
Upsound Lungani 07: 43 I think the unique selling point of Chasing the Sun is the moments before a game in the change room. The team talks at half time, the team talks after certain matches, building up to the final.
17. V/O This all unfolded as the Springboks confronted their arch-rivals, the All Blacks, in the pursuit of rugby's ultimate prize.
18. V/O In a game filled with controversy, South Africa dominated the early stages.
Jesse Kriel 24:24 It wasn't the greatest game of rugby,It was tense
19 V/O But New Zealand showed resilience and found a way back into the game…But the Springboks held on for their fourth World Cup.

Jesse Kriel 24:24 We found a way again and we got the job done. Mzwandile Stick 30:42 That for me was probably lived up to its history when it comes to the Springbok against the All Blacks.
[breather]
20 V/O It's a classic tale of a team from diverse backgrounds, defying the odds. The Springboks not only demonstrated what's achievable but have become a shining example for a nation longing for heroes.
Mzwandile Stick 38:27 Chasing the Sun is Showing You're not only going to unite by winning You know, we need to also show them step-by-step our daily life How do we live amongst each other the respects amongst each other?if you want to change the world can only change what is around you.
Jesse Kriel. I hope there will be a bit of insight on how the coaches thought about their plan and the plan that got presented to us ,I think that is something I am looking forward to because often we are in our heads. Thats what I am looking forward to.
[ end]

metadata.Unique Selling Point: From a sport defined by its past, and a country defined by its differences, comes the story of a team that chooses to believe in something more. “Chasing the Sun” is a powerful SuperSport documentary made in collaboration with the Springboks and tells the rousing tale of their path to redemption and World Cup glory in 2023. The famous triumph remains a powerful memory, but the story behind the famous win is perhaps even more remarkable. SuperSport was granted unprecedented access to the Springboks both in the build-up and during the tournament which helped produce incredible behind-the-scenes footage that goes to the heart of what it took to claim the Webb Ellis Cup last year. “Chasing the Sun” is no ordinary story. It is a story about changing fortunes and changing mindsets, about pressure and hope, about recognizing the power of inspiration, and learning what representation truly means. The moving documentary charts the Boks’ rise f to the pinnacle of international rugby, so vividly demonstrated when captain Siya Kolisi lifted the trophy in France . With unprecedented access and exclusive contributions from coaching staff, players and commentators, the documentary is the story of how a team, a nation and the world came to discover that we are all indeed stronger together. “Chasing the Sun” is infused with humour, technical insights and emotional engagement that will reveal the Springboks like never before.
